skill.name: backend-pr-workflow
skill.description: Review backend pull requests for ClickUp traceability, branch hygiene, release flow, and downtime-safe Django migrations.
skill.summary: Checks backend PR plans against strict branch, ticket, release, and Django migration workflow rules.
skill.author: DiversioTeam

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown inline code and examples, not executable shell or Ruby backtick usage. No prompt injection or automatic command execution was found. One semantic issue remains: the skill should not recommend Slack as a channel for sharing secrets.

remediation.issue: Secret-sharing guidance includes Slack as an acceptable channel.
remediation.suggestion: Change the guidance to require a secrets manager such as 1Password and explicitly avoid posting secrets in Slack or PR descriptions.

### 4.1 Normal release flow (via `release` branch)
- Feature/bugfix PRs merge into `release`.
- The version (e.g. in `pyproject.toml`) is bumped to the intended release
version, using CalVer (e.g. `2025-08-19`).
- If direct pushes to `release` are not allowed, a small PR is created to
bump the version on `release`.
- A PR is created from `release` → `master` with a title like:
- `Release 2: 2025-08-19` (for multiple releases in one day).
- A GitHub Release is created targeting `master`.
- `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DD-2`.
If any of these are obviously missing from the plan, emit `[SHOULD_FIX]`.

content.value_statement: Backend PRs can miss branch rules, ticket links, release steps, or migration safety checks. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured checklist for safer Django backend reviews.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether branch names and PR titles follow ClickUp ticket conventions.
Reviews base branch choice for normal releases and hotfixes.
Assesses PR descriptions for deployment notes, testing notes, and reviewer context.
Flags noisy or unsafe Django migration patterns before merge.
Recommends downtime-safe approaches for schema removals and default backfills.
Formats feedback into aligned items and tagged change requests.
limitations: It relies on user-provided PR details unless the repository is available to inspect.
It does not replace CI, database testing, or human release approval.
Its branch and ticket rules are specific to Diversio-style Django backend workflows.
It gives review guidance but does not automatically create or update pull requests.

use_cases.title: Prepare a backend PR
use_cases.description: Check planned branch name, title, description, and migration summary before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Review migration safety
use_cases.description: Identify Django schema changes that may lock large tables or break running workers during deploy.

use_cases.title: Validate release and hotfix flow
use_cases.description: Confirm target branches, release titles, tags, and merge-back plans match the expected workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Basic PR check
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you have a branch name and PR title.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use backend-pr-workflow to review this backend PR. Branch: <branch>. Base: <base>. Title: <title>. Description: <description>.

prompt_templates.title: Migration review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a PR changes Django models or migrations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use backend-pr-workflow to review these Django model and migration changes for downtime risk. Include blocking and should-fix items.

prompt_templates.title: Hotfix workflow check
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before merging an urgent production fix.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use backend-pr-workflow to check this hotfix plan. Verify the base branch, title, deploy steps, tag plan, and merge-back plan.

prompt_templates.title: Full release readiness review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before a release PR from release to master.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use backend-pr-workflow to perform a full release readiness review. Check included tickets, version bump, release PR title, tag plan, migrations, and deployment notes.

output_examples.input: Review a backend PR with branch feature/auth-cleanup and title Auth cleanup.
output: What is aligned: The description explains the code change.
Needs changes: [BLOCKING] Rename the branch to start with the ClickUp ticket ID.
Needs changes: [BLOCKING] Update the PR title to begin with the ticket ID.

output_examples.input: Review a migration that adds a non-null field with a default on a large table.
output: What is aligned: The PR calls out the schema change.
Needs changes: [BLOCKING] Split the migration into a nullable add, default setup, and batched backfill.
Needs changes: [SHOULD_FIX] Document the deployment order and rollback plan.
What is aligned: The PR clearly describes the production issue.
Needs changes: [BLOCKING] Target master for the hotfix if it must bypass release.
Needs changes: [BLOCKING] Add a plan to merge the deployed fix back into release.

best_practices: Provide the branch name, base branch, PR title, description, and migration summary together.
Include table size and deploy order when asking about migration safety.
Treat blocking findings as required workflow corrections before merge.
anti_patterns: Do not use the same ClickUp ticket across multiple repository PRs.
Do not combine code removal and schema deletion in one risky deploy.
Do not ask for a full review without providing PR context or migration details.

faq.question: Does this skill run migrations or modify code?
faq.answer: No. It reviews plans and repository context, then provides structured workflow guidance.

faq.question: Can it review hotfixes?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks hotfix target branches, release titles, tags, and merge-back expectations.

faq.question: Is it only for Django projects?
faq.answer: The strongest checks are for Django backend repositories, especially migrations and schema deployment safety.

faq.question: Does it require ClickUp?
faq.answer: The branch and PR naming rules assume ClickUp custom ticket IDs. Other teams may need to adapt those rules.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a short summary, aligned items, and tagged needs-change items such as blocking, should-fix, and nit.

faq.question: Can it replace a human reviewer?
faq.answer: No. It helps catch workflow and migration risks before human review, but it does not approve production changes.
